familyTitle: Count in sevens to the 9th number

c.v: Mei counts in sevens: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, and so on.
What is the 9th number she says?
The 9th number in the count is 9 × 7 = 63.
56 is the 8th number and 70 is the 10th number. 16 comes from adding 7 and 9 instead of multiplying.

familyTitle: Next fact from the one before

c.v: 8 × 7 is one more group of 8 than 8 × 6.
54 comes from adding 6 instead of 8. 64 is 8 × 8.

familyTitle: Compare two products

c.v: 56 is greater than 54, so the greater product is 56.

familyTitle: Minutes of reading over several nights

c.v: Hui Min reads for 9 minutes every night. How many minutes does she read in 6 nights?
Each night is 9 minutes. For 6 nights, multiply: 6 × 9 = 54.

familyTitle: Missing number using the fact before

c.v: 6 × 7 is one more group of 6 than 6 × 6.

familyTitle: Wrong multiplier by mistake

c.v: Jun Hao should have multiplied a number by 9.
By mistake, he multiplied it by 7 and got 42.
What answer should he have got?
Step 1: Find his number. He got 42 by multiplying by 7, so the number is 42 ÷ 7 = 6.

familyTitle: Number riddle with 6 and 7 times tables

c.v: I am a number between 30 and 50.
I am in the 6 times table.
When 1 is taken away from me, I am in the 7 times table.
The numbers between 30 and 50 in the 6 times table are 36, 42 and 48.
Only 35 is in the 7 times table (7 × 5 = 35).

familyTitle: Trays of curry puffs in two sessions

c.v: A stall sells curry puffs in trays of 9.
It sells 7 trays in the morning and 6 trays in the afternoon.
How many curry puffs does it sell in the whole day?

familyTitle: Mooncakes packed and not sold

c.v: A bakery packs 8 mooncakes in each box.
It packs 7 boxes on Friday and 9 boxes on Saturday.
15 of these mooncakes are not sold.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the number of mooncakes packed on each day, 56 and 72

familyTitle: Stickers given away then shared onto pages

c.v: Daniel has 9 sheets of stickers. Each sheet has 8 stickers.
He gives 24 stickers to his sister.
He then sticks the rest equally onto 6 pages of his album.
How many stickers are on each page?
Step 2: Stickers left after giving 24 away: 72 − 24 = 48.

familyTitle: Share pencils equally

c.v: How many pencils does each pupil get?
32 and 40 come from taking away 4 or adding 4 instead of dividing.

familyTitle: Number of teams from pupils

c.v: 42 pupils are put into teams of 6.

familyTitle: Groups then balloons

c.v: 30 pupils are put into groups of 5.
How many balloons are given out altogether?
6 is only the number of groups. 90 comes from 30 × 3, which skips the sharing step.

familyTitle: Same number in a times fact and a division fact

c.v: 56 divided by the same number is 8.
From the first sentence: 42 ÷ 6 = 7, so the number is 7.
Check the second sentence: 56 ÷ 7 = 8. It is true.

partialMarks.criterion: Checks it in the other sentence

familyTitle: Think of a number: multiply then add

c.v: I multiply it by 4 and then add 9.
What number did I think of?

familyTitle: Packs of erasers for a class

c.v: Mei needs 35 erasers for her class.
How much does she pay? Give your answer in dollars.

familyTitle: Wheels on tricycles and bicycles

c.v: Each tricycle has 3 wheels. Each bicycle has 2 wheels.
A shop has 6 tricycles and some bicycles.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the wheels on the tricycles, 18
Finds the wheels on the bicycles, 12

familyTitle: Fewer groups when groups are bigger

c.v: 63 pupils are put into groups of 7.
The same pupils are then put into groups of 9 instead.
How many fewer groups are there when the groups have 9 pupils?

familyTitle: Days into weeks

c.v: Mr Lim goes on a holiday for 56 days.

familyTitle: Which number leaves remainder 3

c.v: Which number leaves a remainder of 3 when it is divided by 7?
21 ÷ 7 = 3 with no remainder. 25 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 4. 35 ÷ 7 = 5 with no remainder.

familyTitle: Marbles left over after filling bags

c.v: Ravi puts 29 marbles equally into 4 bags. He puts in as many marbles as he can.
How many marbles are left over?
7 is the number of marbles in each bag, not the number left over.

familyTitle: Balls for full teams only

c.v: 47 children are put into teams of 5.
Every full team is given 2 balls. A team that is not full is given no balls.
How many balls are given out?
Step 1: 47 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 2. There are 9 full teams and 2 children left over.
20 comes from counting the 2 children left over as another team. 94 comes from 47 × 2.

familyTitle: Missing number in a division with remainder
Greatest possible remainder

c.v: What is the greatest possible remainder when a number is divided by 8?
If the remainder were 8, another full group of 8 could be made.
So the remainder must be less than 8. The greatest possible remainder is 7.

familyTitle: Number from quotient and remainder

c.v: The quotient is 8 and the remainder is 5.

familyTitle: Pupils without a team in two classes

c.v: Class 3A makes as many teams of 6 pupils as it can from its 40 pupils.
Class 3B makes as many teams of 7 pupils as it can from its 45 pupils.
Pupils who are left over do not have a team.
How many more pupils have no team in Class 3A than in Class 3B?
Step 1: Class 3A: 40 ÷ 6 = 6 remainder 4. So 4 pupils have no team.
Step 2: Class 3B: 45 ÷ 7 = 6 remainder 3. So 3 pupils have no team.
1 more pupil has no team in Class 3A.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds 4 pupils left over in Class 3A
Finds 3 pupils left over in Class 3B

familyTitle: Day of the week after 30 days

c.v: What day of the week will it be 30 days from today?
There are 7 days in a week, so the days repeat every 7 days.
30 ÷ 7 = 4 remainder 2. After 28 days (4 weeks) it is Monday again.
2 more days after Monday is Wednesday.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the remainder 2 when 30 is divided by 7

familyTitle: Extra books after buying packs

c.v: The books are sold only in packs of 6.
She buys the fewest packs that give her enough books.
How many extra books will she have?
Step 1: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3. 7 packs give only 42 books, which is not enough.

familyTitle: Bottles collected by three classes

c.v: There are 3 classes. Each class collects 238 plastic bottles for recycling.
How many bottles do they collect altogether?
Tens: 3 × 3 = 9, and 9 + 2 = 11. Write 1 and regroup 1 hundred.
614 and 694 come from forgetting to add a regrouped digit.

familyTitle: Grams of rice in packets

c.v: Mrs Lim buys 6 packets of rice. Each packet has 375 g of rice.
How many grams of rice does she buy altogether? Give your answer in grams.

partialMarks.criterion: Multiplies correctly in parts or by the algorithm

familyTitle: Toy robots from the total cost

c.v: Mr Lee paid $469 for some toy robots.
How many toy robots did he buy?
Divide the total cost by the cost of one robot: 469 ÷ 7.
46 tens ÷ 7 = 6 tens with 4 tens left. 4 tens + 9 ones = 49 ones.

familyTitle: Weekly savings over nine weeks

c.v: How much money does he save in 9 weeks? Give your answer in dollars.
56 is 8 weeks of savings and 72 is 8 × 9. 16 comes from adding 9 and 7.

familyTitle: Cookies in two kinds of packets, some eaten

c.v: Mrs Pereira buys 4 packets of 9 cookies and 3 packets of 8 cookies.
How many cookies does she have left?
60 is the answer if she forgets to take away the 5 cookies she ate.

familyTitle: Think of a number: divide then multiply

c.v: I divide it by 6 and then multiply my answer by 7.
What number did I think of?

familyTitle: Spot the error in a times fact

c.v: By how much is his answer wrong?
Sam's answer is 56. The difference is 63 − 56 = 7.

familyTitle: Change after buying pens and files

c.v: Hana buys 6 pens at $3 each and 4 files at $7 each.
How much change does she get? Give your answer in dollars.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds the cost of the pens, $18, and the files, $28

familyTitle: Rows of plants then more rows

c.v: Mr Salim has 72 plants. He puts them equally into 9 rows.
He then plants 5 more rows with the same number of plants in each row.
How many plants does he have altogether?
Step 2: Plants in the 5 new rows: 5 × 8 = 40.

partialMarks.criterion: Finds 40 plants in the 5 new rows

familyTitle: Passengers getting on a bus

c.v: There are 54 passengers on a bus.
At the next stop, 28 more passengers get on.
How many passengers are on the bus now?
Add the tens: 54 + 20 = 74. Then add the ones: 74 + 8 = 82.
There are 82 passengers on the bus.
72 comes from forgetting to regroup 12 ones. 74 comes from adding only the 20.

familyTitle: Number that is less than another

c.v: Work it out in your head.

familyTitle: Cans collected by three classes

c.v: Class 3C collected 28 more cans than Class 3B.
How many more cans did Class 3C collect than Class 3A?
Class 3C collected 6 more cans than Class 3A.

familyTitle: Think of a number: subtract then add

c.v: He subtracts 38 from it and then adds 27.
What number did he think of?

partialMarks.criterion: Undoes the adding of 27 to get 34
